correctness.rationale: The exact-line-search recurrence gives \(x^{(2)}=lpha_0lpha_1[(\mu_0+\mu_1)I-A]b\). For a Stieltjes matrix with condition number at most \(2\), every entry of the bracket is nonnegative because \(\mu_0+\mu_1\ge2\lambda_{\min}\ge\lambda_{\max}\ge a_{ii}\). The sharp family is diagonal and its sign criterion reduces to one exact rational expression. In two dimensions the residual returns after two steps as a scalar multiple with multiplier in \([0,1)\), yielding explicit nonnegative even and odd iterates. The packaged rational checker returns VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: Classical exact-line-search steepest-descent formulas, residual orthogonality, convergence bounds, and Akaike--Forsythe spectral oscillation are treated as prior work. The accepted claim is the coordinatewise Stieltjes second-iterate frontier at condition number \(2\), its sharp all-\(\kappa>2\) three-mode obstruction family, and the all-iterate two-dimensional orthant theorem. Focused semantic and literature searches did not locate an implication-equivalent result.

value.rationale: Stieltjes matrices are a standard class for elliptic discretizations and inverse-positive linear systems. A negative transient coordinate can violate a natural physical or probabilistic sign constraint even while steepest descent decreases the quadratic energy. The sharp conditioning threshold, minimal dimension, earliest failing iterate, and exact witness family give a structural diagnostic rather than a routine restatement of convergence theory.
